_meta.interpretation: It is clearly skewed to the right. Skewness is well above zero, which means a long tail of high earners pulls the average up, and the excess kurtosis is well above zero too, so extreme incomes turn up far more often than a bell curve would predict. The standard deviation is about two thirds of the mean, another sign of a wide, lopsided spread. For a measure shaped like this, report the median beside the mean, and consider a log transform before a test that assumes a bell shape. On a sample of this size a single extreme income can move skewness and kurtosis a lot, so read percentiles or a histogram beside them.
_meta.question: Is customer income skewed, or does it follow a bell curve?
_meta.description: Higher-order distribution-shape moments on customers.pulse income: AGG_STDDEV (spread), AGG_SKEWNESS (asymmetry; m3 / (n * sd^3)), AGG_KURTOSIS (tail-weight; m4 / (n * sd^4) - 3 excess form). Together they form the canonical four-moment shape summary alongside the mean.
